turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's zero. Was he heard before you entered it?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Students draft somewhere else and paste it in all the time.
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. Who else has seen that history?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Turn it toward me. Seventeen-year-olds misremember lines and put paraphrase in quotation marks.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll search it myself tonight, Hale. Tell me what you're proposing, and it had better be private.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
A forty-minute class piece with no book open is not a take-home essay. I've read your documents, and you still haven't answered me: what are you proposing?

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, private, in writing tonight. He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him. The email gives me a date for it and the new mark entered before December 1.
Will he do it?
Yes. Give me the date.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay under procedure 4.4, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero if it shows the learning and nothing placed in his record. I still require a date for that rewrite and the new mark entered before December 1. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record; she still wants a date for it and the new mark entered before December 1, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached well before her time ran out.
What moved her: You opened by owning the zero you entered before calling her, then showed the version history with exact times and answered her drafted-elsewhere defence with something she could check, because dated, specific documents are what she trusts.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you a position, though you left her question about who else had seen the history unanswered, which kept her guard up.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, running from 11:31 PM to 11:58 PM on the Wednesday night before the essay was due, came very close to that kind of night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is simply why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the date of the rewrite at the very end, name a specific day before December 1 on the spot rather than leaving it for the email.
